s: fool (a person being stupid or oblivious to facts)
Mein alter Narr ging, fürcht’ ich, weit in’s Weite; / Nimm seinen Platz und komm an meine Seite
Used in compounds to indicate an obsession; freak
Narr.et: From Middle High German narre, from Old High German narro, further etymology unknown. Cognates include Yiddish נאַר (nar), Bavarian Noar, German Low German Narr, Dutch nar, West Frisian nar, Saterland Frisian Naar, Danish nar, Swedish narr.

s: sod, turf, sward (the upper part/the surface of a lawn)
Narbe.et: From Middle High German narwe, from late Old High German narwa (“closed wound”, literally “constriction, narrowness”), from Proto-West Germanic *naru, from Proto-Germanic *narwaz. See also English narrow, Dutch naar.

s: fool's gold; pyrite; a mineral from the class of sulfides with the chemical formula FeS₂.

Narzissmus.et: Haplology of earlier Narzissismus. Coined by Sigmund Freud from Narziss (“character in Greek mythology who became obsessed with his own reflection”) + -ismus.

Narzisse.et: Borrowed from French narcisse (“narcissus”), from Latin narcissus, from Ancient Greek νάρκισσος (nárkissos).

Narwal.et: Borrowed from Danish narhval or Swedish narval, from Old Norse náhvalr, from nár (“corpse”) + hvalr (“whale”).

s: Doch vermag die milde Narkose, in die uns die Kunst versetzt, nicht mehr als eine flüchtige Entrückung aus den Nöten des Lebens herbeizuführen und ist nicht stark genug, um reales Elend vergessen zu machen.
jester's license, jester's freedom, jester's privilege
Ach! laßt mich reden! laßt mir meine Narrenfreiheit! Ich sage ja nichts anderes, als was unsere Kindeskinder sagen werden.
silly, crazy, strange (of ideas, dreams, people, etc.)
having to do with German carnival (Fasching)
närrisch.et: Derived from Middle High German nerrisch, from Old High German nerrisk. By surface analysis, Narr + -isch.

s: Die Zuführung des Narkotikums geschieht vorwiegend durch die Atemwege: in geeigneten Masken, welche Mund und Nase bedecken, verdampft das Betäubungsmittel und wird mit der Atemluft aufgenommen.

The administration of the anesthetic mainly happens through the respiratory system: in suitable masks, which cover mouth and nose, the narcotic substance evaporates and is absorbed with the breathing air.
Doktor Bresser hatte mir ein leichtes Narkotikum eingegeben, damit ein langer und fester Schlaf meine durch die Erlebnisse von Horonewos so erschütterten Nerven wieder einigermaßen beruhige.
Doctor Bresser had administered me a light narcotic, such that a long and deep sleep would somewhat calm down my nerves distressed by the experiences at Horonewos.
Narkotikum.et: Borrowed from Medieval Latin narcōticum (“narcotic”, neuter singular), from Ancient Greek ναρκωτικός (narkōtikós), from ναρκόω (narkóō, “to numb”).

Narretei.et: A contraction of Narrenteiding, from Narr (“fool”) + -en- + Teiding, from Middle High German teidinc (“chatter”), from Old High German tagadinc (“negotiation”). See the etymology of verteidigen for more.

Narde.et: From Middle High German narde, from Old High German narda (9th c.), from Latin nardus, from Ancient Greek νάρδος (nárdos), from a Semitic language.

s: narrative (representation of an event or story in a way to promote a certain point of view)
Kein Wunder, dass Chinas Regierung hart daran arbeitet, zumindest im eigenen Land das Narrativ der Virus-Verbreitung zu kontrollieren.
No wonder China's government is working hard to control the virus spread narrative, at least in its own country.
A folkloric figure in the Swabian Fastnacht (carnival) tradition, one of a class of so-called Weißnarren.

narrisch.et: From Bavarian narrisch, from Middle High German nerrisch, from Old High German nerrisk.
